title: /audit:version says which build is running and whether a newer one is published
desiredOutcome: one command prints the running version, what the marketplace clone offers and whether it auto-updates, the installed copies, and the newest published release - each with its basis - and says exactly how to update

tasks.title: audit-version.py: the running version, the marketplace and installed copies, and the newest published release
tasks.description: Reads the running build's plugin.json; the marketplace clone and its autoUpdate flag and the installed copies from Claude Code's own records under the Claude home (undocumented files, read with their basis and fail-open); and, unless --offline, the newest GitHub release for plugin.json's repository (one unauthenticated GET, short timeout). Prints each fact with its basis, a verdict, and the documented update commands.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_version.py: each fact with its basis, the verdict, and every read that can fail says why

outcome.technical: met - audit-version.py with basis per fact, fail-open reads, one bounded GitHub call; v1-v11, eight mutations red
outcome.descriptive: A new command reports which version of the plugin is running, what the marketplace offers and whether it updates itself, every installed copy, and the newest published release - and how to update.

tasks.title: The /audit:version command and the surfaces that list commands
tasks.description: commands/version.md; the README command table; the handbook's command reference; SECURITY.md states the one outbound call and what it sends; CHANGELOG.

outcome.technical: met - commands/version.md, README row, handbook entry, SECURITY Outbound network, CHANGELOG
outcome.descriptive: Users can run /audit:version, find it in the command references, and read in SECURITY.md exactly what its one network request sends.
